History: This entry covers the Phoenicians as a people; the trading city-states and their colonies are covered by the Phoenicia entry in Civilizations. The Phoenicians are the coast people of Tyre, Sidon, and Byblos, distinct as a whole from the Sidonians entry, which covers Sidon itself. Hiram, king of Tyre, sent cedar and craftsmen for Solomon's temple (1 Kings 5:1), and a later Tyrian alliance gave Israel Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Zidonians, whose marriage to Ahab imported Baal worship (1 Kings 16:31). Ezekiel's lament over Tyre (Ezekiel 27:2) is the fullest portrait of their trade. In the Gospels Jesus withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21), where a Syrophoenician woman's faith drew his praise (Mark 7:26).
Culture: Seafarers, shipbuilders, and dyers of purple, whose ships carried cedar, metals, and glass across the Mediterranean; their alphabet spread with their trade.
Religion: Baal and Ashtoreth, carried into Israel by Jezebel; Melqart of Tyre, the city god of sailors.
BibleConnection: The Phoenicians are the seafaring traders of the northern coast: Hiram's workmen built Solomon's temple, Jezebel carried their gods into Israel, and Jesus praised a Syrophoenician woman's faith.
RelatedPeople: Hiram, King of Tyre; Jezebel; King Solomon; King Ahab; Elijah

TimePeriod: c. 1200-700 BC as kingdoms; Aramaic remained the region's common language into the New Testament period
Region: Syria, centered on Damascus, with Aramean settlements east and south
History: This entry covers the Arameans as a people; the Damascus-centered kingdoms and their wars are covered by the Aram entry in Civilizations. The Arameans descend from Aram, son of Shem (Genesis 10:22). The King James Version usually calls this people the Syrians: Rebekah was 'the Syrian' (Genesis 25:20), David struck 'the Syrians of Damascus' (2 Samuel 8:5), Ben-Hadad of Syria warred with Ahab (1 Kings 20:1), and Naaman, captain of Syria's army, was healed of leprosy by Elisha (2 Kings 5:1). Amos 9:7 traces the Syrians to Kir. Their language outlived their kingdoms: Aramaic became the Near East's common tongue and remained the everyday speech of Judea in the New Testament period.
Culture: Traders and farmers of the Syrian interior, whose language, Aramaic, spread across the Near East under the empires and was still spoken in Jesus' day.
Religion: Hadadrimmon is named in Zechariah 12:11, though whether the name is a god or a place is debated; Scripture records no Aramean god directly.
BibleConnection: The Arameans are Israel's northern neighbors and rivals: the Syrians of Damascus in Kings, Naaman's people, and the speakers of the Aramaic that became the region's common tongue.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 10:22; Genesis 25:20; 2 Samuel 8:5; 1 Kings 20:1; 2 Kings 5:1; Amos 9:7
RelatedPeople: Hazael, King of Syria; Ben-Hadad I, King of Syria; Naaman; Elisha; King Ahab
RelatedFinds: Melqart Stele; Tel Dan Stele (House of David)

Region: Highlands east of the Dead Sea, between the Arnon and the Zered
History: This entry covers the Moabites as a people; the Moabite kingdom is covered by the Moab entry in Civilizations. The Moabites descend from Moab, born to Lot and his elder daughter (Genesis 19:37). Israel camped in the plains of Moab within sight of the Promised Land (Numbers 22:1), where Balak hired Balaam to curse them. Ruth the Moabitess married into Bethlehem (Ruth 1:4) and became the great-grandmother of David. Mesha's revolt against Israel is recorded both in 2 Kings 3:4 and on his own victory stele, and Isaiah's oracle over Moab (Isaiah 15:1) mourns a people, not only a kingdom.
Culture: Highland farmers and herders east of the Dead Sea, famed for sheep: Mesha's tribute to Israel was a hundred thousand lambs and a hundred thousand rams (2 Kings 3:4).
Religion: Chemosh, god of Moab, to whom Solomon built a high place (1 Kings 11:7) and whose people are called 'the people of Chemosh' (Numbers 21:29).
BibleConnection: The Moabites are Lot's descendants turned neighbor, enemy, and kin: Balak's people, Ruth's people, and the people of Mesha's stele.
RelatedPeople: Ruth; Orpah; Naomi; Boaz; Balak; Balaam; Mesha, King of Moab; Lot; King David

Region: East of the Jordan, around Rabbah
History: This entry covers the Ammonites as a people; the Ammonite state is covered by the Ammon entry in Civilizations. The Ammonites descend from Ben-Ammi, born to Lot and his younger daughter (Genesis 19:38). In the wilderness Israel was told not to take Ammonite land (Deuteronomy 2:19). Jephthah defeated them in the judges era (Judges 11:1), Saul's first victory as king broke Nahash's siege of Jabesh-gilead (1 Samuel 11:1), and David's war with Ammon (2 Samuel 10:1) frames the Bathsheba story. Solomon's many wives included Ammonites (1 Kings 11:1), and their god's high place stood outside Jerusalem until Josiah.
Culture: Farmers and warriors of the Jordan highlands around Rabbah, a walled capital city that held out against Israel's kings.
Religion: Milcom (Molech), the abomination of the Ammonites, to whom Solomon built a high place (1 Kings 11:5, 33).
BibleConnection: The Ammonites are Lot's younger line turned rival: Jephthah's enemy, Saul's first victory, and the war that frames David's fall.
RelatedPeople: Jephthah, Judge of Israel; King Saul; King David; Nahash, King of Ammon; Lot

Region: South of the Dead Sea, from the Arabah to the Red Sea, around Mount Seir
History: This entry covers the Edomites as a people; the Edomite kingdom is covered by the Edom entry in Civilizations. The Edomites descend from Esau, who is Edom (Genesis 36:1), named for the red stew for which he sold his birthright (Genesis 25:30). Edom refused Israel passage in the wilderness (Numbers 20:14), and David put garrisons throughout Edom (2 Samuel 8:14). Obadiah's whole oracle turns on brotherhood betrayed: Edom stood by while strangers carried away Jacob's wealth (Obadiah 1:1). In the later period the same people appear as the Idumeans, whose family produced Herod the Great.
Culture: Miners and traders of the Arabah, working copper and running the Red Sea port of Ezion-geber; in the later period the same people are called Idumeans.
Religion: Edomite inscriptions name Qaus as a national god; Scripture names no Edomite god directly, and the brother-rivalry, not religion, drives the biblical story.
BibleConnection: The Edomites are Esau's people, Israel's brother and rival: the refused passage, the wars of Judah's kings, and Obadiah's oracle against a brother who stood by.
RelatedPeople: Esau; Jacob; King David; Herod the Great
RelatedEvents: Esau Sells His Birthright; Jacob Meets Esau Again

Region: Canaan, then Egypt, then the land of Israel; after the exile, Judah and the Dispersion
History: This entry covers the Israelites as a people; the kingdoms and the whole national story are covered by the Israel entry in Civilizations, and the individual tribes by their own entries. The name comes from Jacob, renamed Israel after wrestling with God (Genesis 32:28); his twelve sons became the twelve tribes. At Sinai the Exodus nation became 'a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation' (Exodus 19:5), 'a holy people unto the LORD thy God' (Deuteronomy 7:6). After Solomon the kingdom split (1 Kings 12:16) and Assyria carried the northern tribes away (2 Kings 17:6), but a remnant returned and the people endured. In the New Testament Paul still opens his anguish with 'my kinsmen according to the flesh: who are Israelites' (Romans 9:4). Whether Paul's 'Israel of God' (Galatians 6:16) means ethnic Israel or the whole church is debated, and is left debated here.
Culture: A tribal people become a nation under Torah: twelve tribes under one covenant, gathered at the tabernacle and then the temple, scattered in exile and regathered under Cyrus.
Religion: The worship of the LORD under the covenant: one God, one Torah, one temple in Jerusalem, the identity that made Israel a people rather than only a kingdom.
BibleConnection: The Israelites are the covenant people of the whole Bible: Jacob's twelve tribes, the Exodus nation, the exiles who returned, and the name Paul still claims in Romans.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 32:28; Exodus 19:5; Deuteronomy 7:6; 1 Kings 12:16; 2 Kings 17:6; Romans 9:4
RelatedPeople: Jacob; Moses; Aaron; Joshua; King David; Abraham; Isaac
RelatedEvents: The Exodus and the Red Sea
